# About Viktor

- Has adjusted commercial losses at Corrigan Hale for 11 years; ran a roofing crew before that
- Handles commercial claims: water, wind, fire, burglary, some premises liability
- Based in Roseville (Sacramento area); bills ~55+ hours/week
- Bills in tenths of an hour for everything, emails and calls included

# Video in Property Claims: Little Use

- Video seldom matters on water, wind or fire losses
  - He sees the damage on site; a loss-day clip only shows what is already obvious
  - Dates a leak from staining and moisture wicking, no footage needed
- Burglary is the exception, and even there the footage changes little
  - Suspects often hooded; payment does not depend on the video
  - Signs of an inside job are for police, not the adjuster
- The pain is moving files, not watching them
  - Clips run under a minute but arrive as folders of large files
  - Shared-drive permissions and corporate IT at Corrigan Hale slow access
  - Carriers still want the footage in the file
- On-site inspection is part of what the carrier owes on large commercial accounts
  - Multi-million premiums; carriers inspect even when not strictly required
  - Inspector expertise catches gaps cameras miss (e.g., a drainpipe giving roof access)

# Biggest Pain: First Reports

- First report ran 10 pages, billed at 0.5 hr/page (5 hours)
- Template-driven, with many details pulled from the policy
- Leans on Copilot and ChatGPT for policy details; they sometimes invent endorsements
  - He doesn't have one tool check another today
- Alex suggested having a second model check the first model's report against the policy

# SiteLog and Partnership

- Building SiteLog, a phone app for the site inspection itself
  - Voice notes, photos and moisture readings become a same-day loss snapshot for the examiner
  - Goal: drying gets approved the day of the visit instead of after the 15-day report
  - Insured gets a same-day note on findings and who is coming
- Examiners are typically assigned ~10 days after a loss; water damage grows meanwhile
- Rough version runs on his phone; voice capture unreliable; no money for a developer
- Expects AI to remove most people from claims handling, soon
- Open to partnering with Acme on SiteLog or on report automation
  - Offered his report template if it is not confidential
- Suggested Acme offer footage review as its own service, handing back just the relevant clip

# To Do

- **Drive up to Roseville to see SiteLog**
- **Send Viktor the two-model cross-check workflow**
